name: Career.io
category: Résumé / career services and outplacement (B2C + enterprise)
positioning: Career.io (formerly Talent Inc., founded 2014) is a portfolio of consumer career brands (TopResume, TopCV, TopInterview, ZipJob, Resume.io, CourseReport) plus enterprise outplacement (Careerminds, PremierVirtual). Sells résumé tools, writing and coaching to individuals and outplacement to 1,000+ enterprise clients.
pricingNote: Not public in sources read; consumer tools are subscription/one-time purchase, enterprise outplacement is contract-based.
hq: New York, NY (press release dateline; HQ not stated)
lastRound: PitchBook lists $13.1M raised; Dealroom lists none; round details unverified
ownership: Private, PE-backed (per PitchBook). Rebranded from Talent Inc. NOT part of Bold (Monster/Zety/LiveCareer) despite some search snippets suggesting that.
headcountSource: Career.io press page 'more than 200 employees worldwide', Aug 2024; aggregators range 11-50 to 1,500 (unreliable)
trafficNote: Similarweb Sept 2026: 370.2K visits over last 3 months; ~123K/month is my average of that figure (estimate). Global rank #102,379.
weWin: Built for laid-off professionals end to end (benefits, funding, WARN-aware), not just documents
AI reskilling courses and workforce-board data/Program workspace
Sold to workforce programs, not only consumers/employers
theyWin: Large résumé brand portfolio and SEO reach, 40M+ résumés generated
Human résumé writers and coaching at scale
partnerIdea: Referral or white-label résumé writing for NextChapter members via TopResume/Resume.io.
notes: Ownership/funding conflict across PitchBook, Dealroom, Prospeo; PitchBook mentions a 2026-02-02 buyout deal with 'Outplacement Australia' that I could not verify. Headcount aggregator figures conflict widely.

name: myOneFlow
positioning: AI-driven case management platform for public service organizations (workforce development, apprenticeship, adult education, public agencies), developed by Empyra. Sells to workforce programs and agencies, not job seekers.
keyFeatures: Case management CRM with digital intake and e-signatures
Enrollment, course payments, attendance and time tracking
pricingNote: Not public; 'Compare Packages' page and demo request.
ownership: Product of Empyra (claims 30+ years in software and consulting); private
weWin: Candidate-facing job search, courses and benefits help
theyWin: Mature WIOA/PIRL compliance reporting and case management
Existing workforce-agency footprint and NAWDP presence
partnerIdea: Integrate NextChapter candidate activity and WARN data into myOneFlow as a data/services feed for Program customers.
notes: Listed in NAWDP marketplace as Jobseekers Solutions, Workforce Solutions, Apprenticeship, but its own site shows it is case-management software for agencies. First search found nothing; site fetch gave the facts.

name: Job Machine
category: AI job placement automation for career schools and workforce orgs
positioning: AI-powered job placement platform for career schools and workforce organizations that creates résumés, submits applications, schedules interviews and tracks employment outcomes at scale.
keyFeatures: Automated reporting for accreditation and federal compliance
Handles hundreds to thousands of candidates without added staff
hq: Austin, TX area code (512) phone; HQ not stated
trafficNote: Similarweb has no data for getjobmachine.com (too small).
weWin: Broader wrap-around: coaching, benefits, funding, reskilling courses
theyWin: Placement/outcome reporting tailored to school accreditation
partnerIdea: Offer NextChapter reskilling and benefits content as an add-on for Job Machine institution customers.
notes: Small vendor; only self-descriptions found (CAPPS Allied Member 2025/2026). Domain also appears as jobmachine.app / jobmachine.pages.dev.

name: Indeed
positioning: World's largest job site; free for job seekers, monetized by employers via sponsored jobs and hiring tools. Also runs Job Search Academy and workforce-system outreach.
keyFeatures: Job Search Academy for workforce professionals
pricingNote: Free for job seekers; employers pay per click/apply (sponsored jobs). Not a flat public price.
ownership: Owned by Recruit Holdings Co., Ltd. (Tokyo)
headcountSource: Not found in this research; Recruit reported a workforce reduction in HR Technology in July 2025 (per search summary)
revenueNote: Reported: Recruit Holdings HR Technology segment (Indeed, Glassdoor and HR Solutions) FY2025 (ended Mar 2026) revenue about US$9.67B, +7.6% YoY; US revenue about $5.31B. This is the segment, not Indeed alone. FY2026 guidance +11.0% to about $10.73B.
trafficNote: Semrush, Sept 2026: 429.42M visits (Aug 425.29M). Similarweb Sept 2026 global rank #57, #1 in US Jobs and Employment.
weWin: Purpose-built for laid-off professionals with coaching and reskilling
weNeed: Employer-verified fresh job supply at scale (we aggregate)
partnerIdea: Position NextChapter as the transition wrap-around alongside Indeed Job Search Academy used by workforce staff.
notes: Revenue figure is a segment and includes Glassdoor and HR Solutions; currency presented as USD in the summary I read (Recruit reports in yen). Headcount not retrieved.

name: CareerOneStop
category: Government career and workforce information portal
positioning: Free suite of websites sponsored by the US Department of Labor (Employment and Training Administration) with career exploration, job search, training, salary and labor-market data, and links to American Job Centers.
revenueNote: Federal funding line for CareerOneStop not found in DOL FY2026 budget search results; not guessed.
trafficNote: Similarweb Sept 2026 shows about 1.4M visits under a 'last 3 months' heading; ~470K/month is my average (estimate). Global rank #28,240.
weWin: Personalized guided journeys, AI tools and coaching
theyWin: Embedded in American Job Centers and state workforce sites
partnerIdea: Cite and link CareerOneStop data inside NextChapter and pitch Program workspace as the personalized layer on top for workforce boards.
notes: Traffic figure ambiguity (3-month vs monthly) noted. Never a paying-buyer competitor; a free public alternative that sets a price floor.
